content:
alex: Noticed p99 jump on /generate for redwood-7b-quant last night ~1.8s (baseline ~0.55s). Correlates with sessions doing long prompts + multi-step tool calls. Sharing logs and quick thoughts.
maria: ugh. any kernel_fallback entries? might be kernel chooser thrashing.
ben: grep shows alternating kernel picks. sometimes attention_fast, sometimes matmul_slow. fallback logs show seq_len_hist mismatch. snippet: ```kernel_choice=attention_fast seq_len=1800 kv_present=true fallback=seq_len_hist```
eva: that smells like microbatch mixing long sessions with short ones so picker recomputes and falls back.
alex: microbatch config: adaptive=true max_microbatch=48 target_ms=200. when a 2k token session arrives batcher tries to include queued short requests -> recompute.
sam: KC: KV hit rate also plummets in these windows. long contexts push eviction and rewarm for the same slot.
infra-bot: metric-snapshot: kv_hit_rate 0.75 -> 0.28 during spike, batch_mean 20 -> 40, p95=430ms, p99=1803ms
maria: ok hypothesis: (1) long prompts + toolcall expansions blow up seq_len & KV footprint; (2) adaptive batch mixes short/long -> kernel picker oscillates; (3) KV eviction + kernel fallback + rewarm => p99 tail.
ben: repro plan: replay synthetic trace (2k prompt + tool loop at 8-12 qps) on probe node; test with microbatching on/off; try kernel pin and session-kv-pin.
eva: starting repro on probe-11: repro-id repro-11/2001.
alex: initial: microbatching=true p99 ~1.75s, microbatching=false (batch=1) p99 ~620ms, kernel_pin attention_fast ~610ms. suggests mixing is the amplifier.
maria: short-term mitigation: batcher should prefer grouping by seq_len_bucket + session affinity TTL so we avoid mixing long followups with unrelated short requests. also expose session_kv_pin for agent flows.
ben: implemented canary: seq_hash_affinity + kv_pin for sessions. rolled to canary slice prod-rg-6.
infra-bot: canary metrics: p99 dropped to ~820ms on slice, kv_hit_rate for agent sessions rose to 0.69, batch_mean reduced slightly.
sam: good fast win. follow-ups for robustness: - precompute kernel from predicted full seq and pin kernel for session until seq_len delta > 30% - background KV rewarm after toolcall returns large payload - reserved-lane for very large sessions to avoid perturbing hot path - perf alert: kernel_fallback_rate > 0.05 -> paged
eva: prototyping reserved-lane on probe-13. objective: keep high-throughput short path untouched.
maria: filing JIRAs: RT-2101 (batcher seq affinity), RT-2102 (session_kv_pin API + metrics), RT-2103 (kernel pin heuristics + counters), RT-2104 (reserved-lane prototype). assigning owners and canary gates.
ben: caveat: kernel pinning might reduce overall throughput for mixed seq traffic. need perf counters and compare token/s across canary.
alex: agree. add microbench harness measuring throughput vs p99 under mixed load.
sam: also add config knob per-customer for token_budget / toolcall depth to avoid runaway agent loops.
maria: ping @oncall if p99 > 1.2s recurrence. I'll update incident doc and attach profiling traces.
infra-bot: incident created INC-2099 linked to RT-2101.
alex: closing thread here. leave implementation details in the JIRAs. :white_check_mark:
